title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
title_bn: ওপেনএআই এর প্রধান বিজ্ঞানী এআই এর উন্নয়নকে কিভাবে সীমাবদ্ধ করা যায় সে বিষয়ে চিন্তাভাবনা করেছেন
author: TechPulse
excerpt: To establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how to measure speed.
paragraph1: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity. Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed.
paragraph2: Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name) could be that measurement. In Pachochki’s argument, benchmarks that focus on AI’s “downstream capabilities” have quickly become outdated as the technology advances. But perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.” Pachochki’s post includes a chart of how the perplexity of OpenAI’s models has fallen since GPT 3.5.
paragraph3: “GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models,” he wrote. “Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.” So in his view, perplexity could provide the basis for “a shared benchmark for general intelligence,” which AI companies could then use to establish “common limits.
paragraph4: ” With perplexity serving as a standard measurement for AI progress, the companies would commit not to go past a certain threshold “until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence. Anthony Ha is TechCrunch’s weekend editor. Previously, he worked as a tech reporter at Adweek, a senior editor at VentureBeat, a local government reporter at the Hollister Free Lance, and vice president of content at a VC firm.
paragraph5: He lives in New York City. You can contact or verify outreach from Anthony by emailing [email protected].
bangla_paragraph1: ওপেনএআই এর প্রধান বিজ্ঞানী জাকব পাচোক্কি এর একটি নতুন ব্লগ পোস্টে এআই উন্নয়নের সম্ভাব্য সীমাবদ্ধতা নিয়ে আলোচনা করা হয়েছে, যার মধ্যে একটি পরিমাপকে বিভ্রান্তি বলা হয়। একজন প্রাক্তন ওপেন এআই এবং এন্থ্রপিক গবেষক বলেন যে কোম্পানিগুলি আমাদের জীবন নিয়ে খেলা করছে, এবং এমনকি এন্থ্ৰপিকের আইপিও ফাইলিংও পরামর্শ দিয়েছে যে প্রযুক্তিটি সমাজের জন্য বিপর্যয়কর বা অস্তিত্বের ঝুঁকি সৃষ্টি করতে পারে। এন্থ্রিকের প্রধান নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা ডারিও আমোদেই তখন একটি পরিকল্পনা প্রকাশ করেছিলেন সীমানা অতিক্রম করতে
bangla_paragraph2: আল্টম্যান দ্বারা বর্ণিত পাচোকির পোস্ট   দীর্ঘ সময়ের মধ্যে ওপেনএআই প্রকাশিত সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ জিনিস  পরামর্শ দেয় যে বিভ্রান্তি (একই নামের সংস্থার সাথে বিভ্রাট করা উচিত নয়) সেই পরিমাপ হতে পারে। পাচোচকি এর যুক্তিতে, এআই  এর  ডাউনস্ট্রিম ক্ষমতা  উপর দৃষ্টি নিবদ্ধ করে এমন বেঞ্চমার্কগুলি দ্রুত প্রযুক্তির অগ্রগতির সাথে সাথে পুরানো হয়ে গেছে। তবে বিভ্রാന്തি  যা  গড় হিসাবে একটি মডেল পরবর্তী টোকেনটি কতটা ভালভাবে পূর্বাভাস দেয় তা পরিমাপ্ত করে; কম বিভ্রাণের অর্থ আরও ভাল পূর্বাভ্যাস
bangla_paragraph3: জিপিটি-৪, ০.৯১-এ, চিন্তাভাবনার চেইন যুক্তিকে উৎপাদনশীলভাবে ব্যবহার করতে দক্ষ ছিল, যা পরবর্তী সময়ে এই ক্ষমতাটির লক্ষ্যবস্তু উদ্দীপনা এবং আধুনিক যুক্তির মডেল তৈরির জন্য অনুপ্রাণিত করেছিল, তিনি লিখেছিলেন। এখন, আমরা ০৮ এর নিচে ক্ষতির দিকে পৌঁছেছি, আমরা সাইবারসিকিউরিটি এবং গণিতের মতো ক্ষেত্রে রূপান্তরমূলক সক্ষমতার উত্থান দেখেছি।
bangla_paragraph4: এআই অগ্রগতির জন্য স্ট্যান্ডার্ড পরিমাপ হিসাবে পরিবেশন করা বিভ্রান্তির সাথে, সংস্থাগুলি একটি নির্দিষ্ট থ্রেশহোল্ড অতিক্রম না করার প্রতিশ্রুতি দেবে  যতক্ষণ না আমাদের এআই আচরণ বোঝার এবং পর্যবেক্ষণ করার ক্ষমতা একটি নির্দিষ্ট নির্দিষ্ট মাইলফলক অর্জন করে। আপনি যখন আমাদের নিবন্ধগুলির লিঙ্কগুলির মাধ্যমে ক্রয় করেন, আমরা একটি ছোট কমিশন উপার্জন করতে পারি। এটি আমাদের সম্পাদকীয় স্বাধীনতাকে প্রভাবিত করে না। অ্যান্টনি হা টেকক্রাঞ্চের উইকএন্ড সম্পাদক। এর আগে তিনি অ্যাডউইকে একজন প্রযুক্তি প্রতিবেদক, ভেঞ্চারবিট, একটি স্থানীয় সরকারের সিনিয়র সম্পাদক হিসাবে কাজ করেছিলেন
bangla_paragraph5: তিনি নিউ ইয়র্ক সিটিতে থাকেন। আপনি [email protected] এ ইমেইল করে অ্যান্টনির সাথে যোগাযোগ করতে বা যোগাযোগের বিষয়টি যাচাই করতে পারেন।

title: The best apps to make new friends right now
title_bn: এই মুহূর্তে নতুন বন্ধু বানানোর জন্য সেরা অ্যাপ
author: TechPulse
excerpt: We've compiled a list of friendship apps, from friend discovery platforms like BFF to event-focused ones like Timeleft.
paragraph1: In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent. In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General went so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interactions found in an office, and younger individuals eager to create their adult social circles based on shared interests and hobbies, are among those seeking meaningful friendships. Thanks to online dating apps, the stigma associated with finding connections online has largely faded away. This has welcomed a new wave of apps focused on fostering friendships and building local communities. According to estimates from Appfigures, over a dozen local-focused friendship apps have collectively generated approximately $16 million in consumer spending in the U.S. so far this year. Some notable examples include Timeleft, Meet5, and Bumble’s BFF. Additionally, these apps have garnered approximately 4.3 million downloads thus far in 2025. The apps aim to provide a less awkward solution than, for instance, approaching a stranger at the gym or local café and trying to strike up a conversation. These platforms clearly indicate that everyone using the app is looking for the same thing — friendship, not romance — making it much less intimidating to initiate conversations. From major players like Meetup to newer ones like 222, there are plenty of apps that cater to the growing demand for meaningful friendships.
paragraph2: We’ve compiled a list of them for you to try out. 222 Image Credits:222 (screenshot) The app 222 is an iOS-only social events platform that facilitates in-person meetups by pairing a group of strangers based on their personality test results. The app sends invitations to nearby public social events, such as wine bars and comedy clubs. There is then a vetting process, and selected participants are notified on the day of the event. A bonus for those who feel socially anxious: You’re allowed to bring a plus-one. The service charges a $22.22 curation fee or a monthly subscription for the same price. Bumble BFF Image Credits:Bumble Dating giant Bumble is among the more established players to enter the friendship space, launching its friend-finding feature in 2016, which then spun out into a stand-alone app in 2023. The friend-making app has recently undergone a significant redesign, with an increased emphasis on facilitating group meetups, catering to users’ desires to grow their social circles. BFF is available for free download on iOS and Android devices. Clyx Image Credits:Clyx Clyx is another emerging app in the group-based social networking landscape, with a strong focus on discovering local events. The social platform helps users find community events by integrating data from platforms like Ticketmaster and TikTok. Additionally, Clyx allows users to upload their contact lists, helping them see which events their friends plan to attend. The app also includes a feature that recommends other users to connect with at these events. As of now, Clyx operates exclusively in two cities: Miami and London. However, it has plans to expand to additional areas in the near future, with New York City and São Paulo at the top of the list.
paragraph3: The app is available on the App Store and Google Play Store. Crowdier Image Credits:Crowdier Crowdier is a new group social app that lets friend groups connect with others. Users can create a group of 2-5 friends and browse other groups to arrange hangouts in person. To initiate a match, users can “Wave” at groups they like, and if those groups wave back, they can plan in a shared chat. A match requires the majority of both groups to agree. For example, 2 people in a 4-person group needs to say yes. The app is available for free on iOS and Android devices. Les Amís Image Credits:Les Amis Les Amís is a friendship app tailored for women, transgender, and LGBTQ+ individuals that leverages AI to match users based on similar interests and encourages participation in local events, such as pottery classes, book clubs, and wine tastings. Matches are made every Monday, allowing users to chat and plan meetups later in the week. Available on iOS and Android, Les Amís serves cities across Europe, including Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Madrid, Paris, and Stockholm. In the U.S., the app is available in Austin and New York, with plans to expand to Boston, Miami, and Los Angeles. The app uses a paid membership model that varies by city, with fees of $70 in New York and €55 in Amsterdam. Meetup Image Credits:Meetup The local event-discovery platform has been around since 2002, helping millions of users connect with others who share similar interests. Users can RSVP to events; join groups that cater to a variety of hobbies, professions, or social causes; and create their own groups and events.
paragraph4: They can also chat with group members and post updates and photos from gatherings. Meet5 Image Credits:Meet5 This European community-building app recently launched in the U.S., targeting users over 40 who want to meet new people in their area and participate in group activities such as picnics, concerts, and hiking. Notably, in a short time, there have been around 777,000 U.S. downloads so far across the App Store and Google Play Store, according to Appfigures estimates. Pie Image Credits:Pie Pie is another one of the newer social apps on the market. It features an AI-driven quiz designed to predict which users are most likely to be compatible with each other. Each person who RSVPs to a Pie event takes a brief personality assessment, and the algorithm organizes attendees into groups of six, who are then added to a group chat within the Pie app, allowing them to interact with each other before the event. Currently, the app is only available in Austin, Chicago, and San Francisco. Users can download Pie from the App Store and Google Play Store. Timeleft Image Credits:Timeleft Timeleft is a relatively new platform that helps you organize weekly dinner dates with groups of strangers. The app uses a special algorithm to match you with others, taking into account your age, gender, and personality. Users are matched with four other people, but they only learn minor details about them the night before, including their occupations and zodiac signs. Dinners take place at a selected restaurant on Wednesday evenings at 7:00 p.
paragraph5: m. To help everyone break the ice, the app offers a game with conversation starters. After dinner, there is an after-party at a local bar. Users can book dinners online or through the app. In terms of pricing, it varies depending on the country and restaurant. Users pay for a ticket up front and are responsible for covering their own dinner and drinks. Washed Up Image Credits:Washed Up Washed Up is a social event discovery app that launched in early 2026, designed for people in the Los Angeles area who want an easier way to find things to do and meet new people. The app helps users discover local events, such as concerts, trivia nights, and comedy shows, while also giving them a built-in way to connect with others who plan to attend. Instead of going to events alone, users can create or join “plans,” which are small group meetups tied to specific events. Users can browse these plans and request to join, chat with the group, and add new friends, making it easier to show up to events with people rather than by themselves. It’s available to download on the App Store. Wyzr Friends Image Credits:Wzyr Friends Wyzr Friends is an activity-based friendship app designed for adults 40 and older, catering to empty nesters, those who are divorced, and other users seeking to connect with like-minded individuals. Users can thumbs up or down potential friends and arrange in-person activities based on shared interests, such as going to the movies or hiking.
bangla_paragraph1: সাম্প্রতিক বছরগুলিতে, মানুষ প্লাটোনিক সংযোগ গঠনের নতুন উপায়গুলির সন্ধান করছে, কারণ একাকীত্ব এবং সামাজিক বিচ্ছিন্নতা আরও প্রচলিত হয়ে উঠেছে। ২০২৩ সালে, মার্কিন সার্জন জেনারেল এই বিষয়টিকে জনস্বাস্থ্য সংকট হিসাবে চিহ্নিত করার মতো দূরবর্তী যান। দূরবর্তী কর্মীরা, যারা অফিসে পাওয়া প্রতিদিনের মিথস্ক্রিয়া মিস করেন এবং যৌবনের ব্যক্তিরা ভাগ করে নেওয়া আগ্রহ এবং শখের উপর ভিত্তি করে তাদের প্রাপ্তবয়স্ক সামাজিক বৃত্ত তৈরি করতে আগ্রহী, যারা অর্থপূর্ণ বন্ধুত্বের সন্ধান করছেন তাদের মধ্যে রয়েছে। অনলাইন ডেটা এর জন্য ধন্যবাদ
bangla_paragraph2: আমরা আপনার জন্য তাদের একটি তালিকা সংকলন করেছি। 222 চিত্র ক্রেডিটঃ 222 (স্ক্রিনশট) অ্যাপ 222 একটি আইওএস-কেবল সামাজিক ইভেন্ট প্ল্যাটফর্ম যা তাদের ব্যক্তিত্ব পরীক্ষার ফলাফলের উপর ভিত্তি করে অপরিচিতদের একটি গ্রুপকে জোড়া দিয়ে ব্যক্তিগত সাক্ষাতের সুবিধার্থে। অ্যাপটি কাছাকাছি পাবলিক সামাজিক ইଭେন্টগুলিতে আমন্ত্রণ পাঠায়, যেমন ওয়াইন বার এবং কমেডি ক্লাব। তারপরে একটি ভেটিং প্রক্রিয়া রয়েছে এবং নির্বাচিত অংশগ্রহণকারীদের ইভেন্টে জানানো হয়। সামাজিকভাবে উদ্বিগ্ন বোধকারীদের জন্য একটি বোনাসঃ আপনাকে ব্রাই করার অনুমতি দেওয়া হয়।
bangla_paragraph3: অ্যাপটি অ্যাপ স্টোর এবং গুগল প্লে স্টোরে উপলব্ধ। ক্রাউডিয়ার চিত্র ক্রেডিটঃক্রাউডিয়র ক্রাউডার একটি নতুন গ্রুপ সামাজিক অ্যাপ্লিকেশন যা বন্ধু গোষ্ঠীগুলিকে অন্যদের সাথে সংযোগ করতে দেয়। ব্যবহারকারীরা ২-৫ জন বন্ধুদের একটি গ্রুপ তৈরি করতে এবং ব্যক্তিগতভাবে হ্যাংআউটগুলি সাজানোর জন্য অন্যান্য গোষ্ঠীতে ব্রাউজ করতে পারেন। একটি ম্যাচ শুরু করতে, ব্যবহারকারীগণ তাদের পছন্দসই গোষ্ঠীর কাছে  ওয়েভ করতে পারেন এবং যদি সেই গোষ্ঠীরা ফিরে আসে তবে তারা একটি ভাগ করা চ্যাটে পরিকল্পনা করতে পারে। একটি ম্যাচের জন্য উভয় গোষ্ঠির সংখ্যাগরিষ্ঠের সম্মতি প্রয়োজন। উদাহরণস্বরূপ, ৪ জনের গ্রুপের ২ জনকে  বলতে হবে।
bangla_paragraph4: তারা গ্রুপের সদস্যদের সাথে চ্যাট করতে এবং সমাবেশ থেকে আপডেট এবং ফটো পোস্ট করতে পারে। Meet5 Image Credits:Meet5 এই ইউরোপীয় সম্প্রদায়-বিল্ডিং অ্যাপ্লিকেশনটি সম্প্রতি মার্কিন যুক্তরাষ্ট্রে চালু করা হয়েছে, যা 40 বছরের বেশি বয়সী ব্যবহারকারীদের লক্ষ্য করে যারা তাদের এলাকায় নতুন লোকের সাথে দেখা করতে এবং পিকনিক, কনসার্ট এবং হাইকিংয়ের মতো গ্রুপ ক্রিয়াকলাপে অংশ নিতে চান। উল্লেখযোগ্যভাবে, অল্প সময়ের মধ্যে অ্যাপ স্টোর এবং গুগল প্লে স্টোরে এখন পর্যন্ত প্রায় 777,000 মার্কিন ডাউনলোড হয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph5: m. সবার বরফ ভাঙতে সাহায্য করার জন্য, অ্যাপটি কথোপকথন শুরু করার সাথে একটি গেম সরবরাহ করে। রাতের খাবারের পরে, স্থানীয় একটি বারে একটি পার্টি হয়। ব্যবহারকারীরা অনলাইন বা অ্যাপের মাধ্যমে ডিনার বুক করতে পারেন। মূল্য নির্ধারণের ক্ষেত্রে, এটি দেশ এবং রেস্তোঁরাটির উপর নির্ভর করে পরিবর্তিত হয়। গ্রাহকরা একটি টিকিটের জন্য আগাম অর্থ প্রদান করেন এবং তাদের নিজস্ব ডিনারের এবং পানীয়ের জন্য দায়বদ্ধ। ওয়াশ আপ চিত্র ক্রেডিটঃওয়াশ আপ ওয়াশআপ একটি সামাজিক ইভেন্ট আবিষ্কার অ্যাপ যা 2026 সালের প্রথম দিকে চালু হয়েছিল, যা লস অ্যাঞ্জেলেসের লোকদের জন্য ডিজাইন করা হয়েছিল।

paragraph1: An experimental iPhone Duo interface tested by Apple would allow widgets to occupy two separate areas of the Lock Screen, according to findings shared by the leaker known as "pdfu." The unreleased layout adds a vertical pair of circular widgets on the right side of the screen. Crucially, pdfu says this arrangement can be used together with the existing bottom row, giving users access to more information. Apple has tested a "complication column" for iPhone Duo's Lock Screen.
paragraph2: It fits two circular widgets along the right edge. — pdfu (@itspdfu) November 22, 2026 Called a "Complication Column," the additional widget area sits above the customizable shortcuts normally assigned to the flashlight and camera. Network status indicators remain above it, with the widgets making use of the intervening space. The widget column is disabled for now.
paragraph3: According to pdfu, it is controlled by an internal "SpringBoard/Ionic" setting and was first identified in iOS 27.1. No subsequent changes to its code have been spotted, so it is not clear whether Apple is still developing it or plans to make it available in the future. paragraph1: Apple's recent Siri layoffs affected employees working on the assistant's older infrastructure rather than its newer AI systems, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. In his latest "Power On" newsletter, Gurman said employees have yet to notice a major difference in how Apple operates despite efforts to accelerate development and spread significant releases throughout the year. He added that the company faces growing competition from AI developers that update their models and services far more frequently than Apple's annual operating system cycle. Within software engineering chief Craig Federighi's organization, Apple apparently follows an internal release calendar labeled A through G, with engineering work tied to specific software versions and launch windows.
paragraph2: Depending on the release, the roadmap and features for a major operating system update are largely determined by late summer or early fall of the preceding year. Gurman argued that this structure leaves Apple with limited flexibility to respond to competitors' breakthroughs during the subsequent development cycle. Gurman also criticized ‌Siri‌'s slow responses, limited third-party integration, and seemingly worsening dictation. Apple is reportedly developing a more advanced AI agent, but Gurman does not expect it to arrive before late 2027.
paragraph3: He warned that rival agents could become difficult to abandon as they accumulate users' preferences and connected accounts, although Apple's reputation for privacy and deeper platform access could help it compete. ‌Siri‌'s multistep control of Apple apps is expected to launch in December, with third-party app support following in 2027. bangla_paragraph3: তিনি সতর্ক করেছিলেন যে প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বী এজেন্টগুলি ব্যবহারকারীদের পছন্দ এবং সংযুক্ত অ্যাকাউন্টগুলি জমা দেওয়ার সাথে সাথে পরিত্যাগ করা কঠিন হয়ে উঠতে পারে, যদিও গোপনীয়তা এবং গভীর প্ল্যাটফর্ম অ্যাক্সেসের জন্য অ্যাপলের খ্যাতি এটিকে প্রতিযোগিতায় সহায়তা করতে পারে। অ্যাপল অ্যাপ্লিকেশনগুলির সিরির বহু-পদক্ষেপ নিয়ন্ত্রণ ডিসেম্বরে চালু হওয়ার আশা করা হচ্ছে, তৃতীয় পক্ষের অ্যাপ্লিকেশনের সমর্থন 2027 সালে অনুসরণ করবে। জনপ্রিয় গল্পঅ্যাপল আইফোন ডুওকে চারটি উপায়ে আপগ্রেড করার লক্ষ্য রাখেরবিবার, নভেম্বর 15, 2026 সকাল 8:42 পিএসটি জো রসসাইনলব্লুমবার্গের মার্ক গারম্যান আজ বলেছেন অ্যাপল হ
bangla_paragraph4: অ্যাপল আইওএস ২৮ এবং ম্যাকোস ২৮ এর বিকাশের জন্য নতুন পদ্ধতি গ্রহণ করেছেব্লুমবার্গের মার্ক গুরম্যানের মতে, অ্যাপল তার আইওএস ২8, ম্যাকস ২8 এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট সফ্টওয়্যার আপডেটের জন্য তার বিকাশ প্রক্রিয়াতে পরিবর্তন এনেছে। আজ তার পাওয়ার অন নিউজলেটারটিতে তিনি বলেছিলেন যে অ্যাপল প্রতিবছর নতুন অপারেটিং সিস্টেমগুলির বিকাশকে তিনটি প্রধান পর্যায়ে আলাদা করে। সাধারণত তিনি বলেছিলেন প্রতিটি পর্যায়ে কোডিংয়ের চার সপ্তাহের একটি চার সপ্তাহ "সংকোচন" সময়কাল রয়েছে যেখানে...তিনটি নতুন আইপ্যাড গুজব প্রথমার্ধে চালু হবে।

title: 17-year-old Windows 7 gets unofficial DirectX 12 and Vulkan 1.4 support
title_bn: ১৭ বছরের উইন্ডোজ ৭ এর অ-অফিসিয়াল ডাইরেক্টএক্স ১২ এবং ভুলকান ১.৪ সমর্থন পেয়েছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A community-developed project brings DirectX 12 and Vulkan 1.4 support to Microsoft's retired operating system, allowing modern Nvidia, AMD, and Intel graphics cards to work with Windows 7.
paragraph1: Windows 7 may have been retired years ago, but that hasn’t stopped enthusiasts from finding ways to bring modern hardware and features to Microsoft’s beloved operating system. A new community project is now giving Windows 7 the ability to support modern Nvidia, AMD, and Intel graphics cards, along with DirectX 12 and Vulkan 1.4 capabilities.
paragraph2: Developed by enthusiasts EAZY BLACK, kryptik, and VisualEhrmanntraut, the project backports WDDM 2.2 from Windows 10. Interestingly, Windows 7 originally launched with WDDM 1.
paragraph3: 1, while Microsoft introduced WDDM 2.0 with Windows 10 in 2015 and WDDM 2.2 with the Creators Update in 2017.
paragraph4: Microsoft also introduced a limited version of DirectX 12 for Windows 7 in 2019; however, that implementation was only meant for developers to port select games to the older operating system.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
bangla_paragraph1: উইন্ডোজ ৭ হয়তো কয়েক বছর আগে অবসর গ্রহণ করেছে, কিন্তু এটি মাইক্রোসফটের প্রিয় অপারেটিং সিস্টেমে আধুনিক হার্ডওয়্যার এবং বৈশিষ্ট্য আনতে উপায় খুঁজে পেতে উত্সাহীদের বাধা দেয়নি। একটি নতুন সম্প্রদায় প্রকল্প এখন উইন্ডজ ৭ কে আধুনিক এনভিডিয়া, এএমডি এবং ইন্টেল গ্রাফিক্স কার্ডগুলি সমর্থন করার ক্ষমতা দিচ্ছে, ডাইরেক্টএক্স ১২ এবং ভুলকান ১.৪ সক্ষমতার সাথে।
bangla_paragraph2: এজেডি ব্ল্যাক, ক্রিপ্টিক এবং ভিজ্যুয়াল ইহরমানট্রাউট এর উত্সাহীদের দ্বারা বিকাশিত, প্রকল্পটি উইন্ডোজ 10 থেকে ডাব্লুডিডিএম 2.2 সমর্থন করে। মজার বিষয় হল, উইন্ডজ 7 মূলত ডাব্লিউডিডিএমের সাথে চালু হয়েছিল।
bangla_paragraph3: 1, যখন মাইক্রোসফ্ট ২০১৫ সালে উইন্ডোজ ১০ এর সাথে ডাব্লুডিডিএম ২.০ এবং ২০১৭ সালে ক্রিয়েটর আপডেটের সাথে ডব্লিউডিডিএমই ২.২ চালু করেছিল।
bangla_paragraph4: মাইক্রোসফট 2019 সালে উইন্ডোজ 7 এর জন্য ডাইরেক্টএক্স 12 এর একটি সীমিত সংস্করণও চালু করেছিল; তবে, এই বাস্তবায়নটি কেবলমাত্র ডেভেলপারদের পুরানো অপারেটিং সিস্টেমে নির্বাচিত গেমগুলি পোর্ট করার জন্য বোঝানো হয়েছিল। টমস হার্ডওয়্যারের সেরা সংবাদ এবং গভীর পর্যালোচনাগুলি সরাসরি আপনার ইনবক্সে পান।

paragraph1: In his new book “Hyperscale,” journalist Paris Marx investigates the impact of data centers and generative AI, taking readers inside the data centers themselves and explaining how computing infrastructure that goes back decades recently became a political landmine. The book is well-timed, to put it mildly, as data center backlash seems to have been one of the motivators for the massive blue wave seen in the recent midterm elections. And those debates are likely to continue as Democrats wield more governmental power. In an interview with TechCrunch, Marx described the data center buildout as “fundamentally unsustainable” and “completely out of line with a livable planet,” while also arguing that these facilities make for an obvious target amidst broader anger at the tech industry. After all, if a data center is being built in your community, “it’s very physical, it’s very material.” “It doesn’t matter what side of the political spectrum that you’re on,“ Marx said. “You are going to feel the effects of that in your quality of life, in your power bill, potentially in your access to water, potentially in what you hear around your community, if these air conditioning units on the roofs of data centers are making a lot of noise.” He also suggested that data center opposition is only the most visible piece of a wider movement targeting “the physical manifestations of the tech industry, […] whether it’s the opposition to Flock cameras rolling out across the United States, or the smart glasses that Meta is trying to put on people’s faces, or even the self-driving cars that Waymo is rolling out.” During our conversation (which I’ve edited for length and clarity), Marx and I discussed data centers’ environmental impact, how tech companies are responding to community resistance, and what it’s actually like inside a data center. I liked your description of trying to get access to the inside of a “hyperscale” data center and then eventually taking a tour [of one]. Could you talk a little bit more about what that experience was like?
paragraph2: How did you get in? What surprised you when you actually got in? Getting inside of a hyperscale data center was not the easiest task in the world. I spoke to some researchers who have been doing research on data centers for a number of years longer than I had, and they told me that before the generative AI moment, and before all the attention that has been put on data centers recently, that it was quite a bit easier to do so. I sent emails to a number of companies asking if I could get inside, often didn’t get a response, other times got a no. I ended up, after visiting the outsides of some data centers in places like northern Virginia and Ireland and spots like that, I actually went down to New Zealand to go inside of a data center itself. And the thing that struck me most was the level of security. Obviously, you would expect that this is an infrastructure that is really securitized, because the data inside needs to be kept safe, obviously [they] have these big fences and all the security cameras around the data centers. But to go inside, I had to send my passport in advance. Then when I got there, they had to check the passport, and then as we were going through the data center itself, every single door in the data center was locked unless you had a key card to unlock it. Then, when you get inside of the server room itself, where all this computer hardware is stored in tall racks that look like cabinets — you can imagine, in your mind, that this would be kind of a sinister location, with some eerie lighting or something like that.
paragraph3: But in truth, it’s just quite utilitarian. It’s a warm room with some air conditioning blasting into the servers from vents that are nearby. It was really loud as well, because you have all these fans running from all these servers, it was really kind of piercing. To be inside of this room, if you were going to be in there for a while, you’d probably want earplugs or something like that. Before I read your book, I thought of data centers as something that’s important, but a little bit boring. How did you decide they were interesting and rich enough to sustain an entire book? I felt the same. I was aware that data centers had been out there, but it was not something that I was paying particularly close attention to. But then there were a number of stories that of tipped me off to the fact that there might be more here, and that it was worth looking deeper into what was going on — the first being hearing about the water pressures created by data centers in Chile around the capital of Santiago, where companies like Google and Microsoft were building data centers, and communities were concerned about their access to water and started organizing around that. And then hearing about how much electricity data centers were consuming in Ireland, to the point that now they consume more than 20% of the country’s electricity, and that was obviously pushing up power prices. It was putting pressures on the grid, such that the grid operator actually put a moratorium in place for grid connections for data centers around the Dublin area, back in 2022.
paragraph4: This was even before the generative AI moment that caused a surge in construction of data centers. And then the other one was in The Dalles, Oregon, where Google had actually built its first company-owned data centers about 20 years back. In that case, its water deal was coming up for renewal. It wanted to build more data centers there, so it needed more water. And when the residents started asking, “How much water is Google actually using?” a journalist at The Oregonian went to the city and essentially asked, “Hey, how much water is Google using? Our readers would like to know this,” he was hit with a lawsuit instead of being given that information. Because Google did not want it to be public. And then, of course, when it did come out about a year later, Google revealed that it was using 29% of the city’s water, which seemed quite significant. That was around when ChatGPT was being released and generative AI was starting to take off. It felt like, okay, there are these pockets of places where a lot of data centers have already been constructed, where they are putting pressures on the communities that are causing people to respond, and it felt like that was going to start coming to a lot more communities.
paragraph5: It was a good time to really start to dig in and pay attention. You don’t just talk about the data centers’ environmental impact, but also, they [become] your way in to talk about this broader tech moment. They represent to you — particularly the hyperscale data centers — represent to you how these tech companies are doing business now. Absolutely. The hyperscale data centers and just the scale of the construction — whether it’s the the size of the actual facilities themselves or the number that these companies are trying to build out, just feels fundamentally unsustainable. They’re just demanding too much from the communities where they’re being located, whether that’s because of electricity or because of water use or what have you, or just the fact that they’re building out so many, that when you think about the cumulative impact and you look at the demand for water, but particularly for energy from fossil fuels, that means that it’s just completely out of line with a livable planet and an amount of computation that feels like it makes any degree of sense for us to have constructed. I think it really goes back to the hubris of the tech industry and of these major tech companies and the tech billionaires that run them, and the fact that they have these particular visions of the future that are based on fantasies, but also on expanding their own power and influence over the world, and they don’t seem to mind that everyone else then has to pay the cost that comes with their ambitions and what they are seeking to do.

bangla_paragraph2: আপনি কিভাবে প্রবেশ করলেন? আসলে আপনি যখন প্রবেশ করলেন তখন আপনাকে কী অবাক করে? হাইপারস্কেল ডেটা সেন্টারের ভিতরে প্রবেশ করা বিশ্বের সবচেয়ে সহজ কাজ ছিল না। আমি কিছু গবেষকের সাথে কথা বলেছি যারা আমার চেয়ে কয়েক বছর বেশি সময় ধরে ডেটা কেন্দ্রগুলিতে গবেষণা করে আসছেন, এবং তারা আমাকে বলেছিল যে জেনারেটিভ এআই মুহুর্তের আগে, এবং সাম্প্রতিক সময়ে ডেটা কেন্দ্রে যে সমস্ত মনোযোগ দেওয়া হয়েছে, তার আগে এটি করা বেশ সহজ ছিল। আমি বেশ কয়েকটি সংস্থার কাছে ইমেল পাঠিয়েছিলাম যে আমি ভিতরে যেতে পারি কিনা,
bangla_paragraph3: কিন্তু সত্য, এটা খুবই উপযোগী। এটা একটা উষ্ণ ঘর যেখানে এয়ার কন্ডিশনার আছে, যা সার্ভারে প্রবেশ করে। এটা খুব জোরেও ছিল, কারণ এই সার্ভারের সব ফ্যানের ভেতর দিয়ে খুব জোরাজুরি চলছে। এটা সত্যিই খুব আঘাতমূলক। এই রুমের ভেতরে যদি আপনি কিছুক্ষণ থাকবেন, তাহলে সম্ভবত আপনার কানের প্লাগ লাগবে। আপনার বইটি পড়ার আগে আমি ডাটা সেন্টারকে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ, কিন্তু কিছুটা বিরক্তিকর কিছু মনে করতাম।
bangla_paragraph4: এটি এমন একটি সময় ছিল যখন ডেটা সেন্টার নির্মাণের ক্ষেত্রে প্রবৃদ্ধি ঘটেছিল। এবং তারপর অন্যটি ছিল দ্য ডালস, ওরেগনে, যেখানে গুগল প্রায় ২০ বছর আগে তার প্রথম কোম্পানি মালিকানাধীন ডেটা কেন্দ্র তৈরি করেছিল। সেই ক্ষেত্রে, তার জলের চুক্তি পুনর্নবীকরণের জন্য আসছিল। তারা সেখানে আরও ডেটা কেন্দ্রে নির্মাণ করতে চেয়েছিল, তাই তাদের আরও জলের প্রয়োজন ছিল। এবং যখন বাসিন্দারা জিজ্ঞাসা করতে শুরু করেছিল, গল আসলে কত জল ব্যবহার করছে? দ্য ওরেজোনীয়ানের একজন সাংবাদিক শহরে গিয়েছিলেন এবং বলেন
bangla_paragraph5: এটা সত্যিই গভীরভাবে খুঁজতে এবং মনোযোগ দিতে শুরু করার জন্য একটি ভাল সময় ছিল। আপনি শুধু ডাটা সেন্টার পরিবেশগত প্রভাব সম্পর্কে কথা বলতে না, কিন্তু এছাড়াও, তারা এই বৃহত্তর প্রযুক্তি মুহূর্ত সম্পর্কে কথা বলার জন্য আপনার উপায় হয়ে. তারা আপনাকে প্রতিনিধিত্ব করে  বিশেষ করে হাইপারস্কেল ডেটা সেণ্টার  আপনাকে প্রতিনিধি কিভাবে এই প্রযুক্তি কোম্পানি এখন ব্যবসা করছে। একেবারে. হাইপারস্কেল ডেটা কেন্দ্র এবং শুধু নির্মাণের স্কেল  কিনা এটা  প্রকৃত সুবিধা নিজেদের আকার বা সংখ্যা যে

title: How to use auto drive in GTA 6? What does it do? Does it work with boats in the video game? All questions answered
title_bn: জিটিএ ৬-এ অটো ড্রাইভ কিভাবে ব্যবহার করবেন? এটি কি করে? এটি ভিডিও গেমের নৌকা দিয়ে কাজ করে? সমস্ত প্রশ্নের উত্তর দেওয়া হয়েছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Grand Theft Auto VI’s Auto-Drive feature lets Jason or Lucia travel to a waypoint while players enjoy cinematic views. Available in road vehicles and boats, it still takes time and may struggle with obstacles, so it is best for relaxed journeys rathe
paragraph1: Grand Theft Auto VI’s Auto-Drive feature lets Jason or Lucia travel to a waypoint while players enjoy cinematic views. Available in road vehicles and boats, it still takes time and may struggle with obstacles, so it is best for relaxed journeys rather than pursuits or demanding maneuvers.How to use auto drive in GTA 6? What does it do? Does it work with boats? (Images: Bloomberg, File photo)Grand Theft Auto VI has introduced an Auto-Drive feature that allows players to travel across Leonida without having to manually steer their vehicles. The feature can take control of a car and navigate towards a destination selected on the map, giving players the option to enjoy the game's surroundings while Jason or Lucia handles the journey.The feature is particularly useful for longer trips across Vice City and other parts of Leonida, where travelling between locations can take time. Auto-Drive is integrated into the game's Cinematic Mode, which switches between different camera angles while the vehicle is moving.According to gaming guides Beebom and GTA6.house, players can activate the feature by setting a waypoint, entering Cinematic Mode and using the appropriate controller button.How to activate Auto-Drive in GTA 6?Players need to follow a few steps to let the game's artificial intelligence take over driving duties.
paragraph2: 2. Get inside a vehicle and open the in-game map.3. Select the destination and place a waypoint.4. Start driving and hold the Down button on the D-pad to access the camera options.5. Press the Options button on PlayStation or Menu on Xbox to enter Cinematic Mode.6. Once the Auto-Drive prompt appears, hold Circle on PlayStation or B on Xbox to activate the feature.Once enabled, Jason or Lucia will automatically drive towards the selected destination. Players can also adjust the vehicle's speed using L2 and R2 on PlayStation or LT and RT on Xbox.To return to manual driving, players can exit Cinematic Mode using the Down button on the D-pad.
paragraph3: What does Auto-Drive do in GTA 6?Auto-Drive allows players to hand over control of their vehicles to the game's driving AI. Instead of continuously steering, accelerating and braking, players can let the character follow the route towards the selected waypoint.The feature is designed to make longer journeys less demanding and allow players to experience the game's cinematic driving sequences. The AI generally follows traffic rules and stops at traffic signals rather than driving recklessly.However, Auto-Drive is not the same as fast travel. The vehicle still needs to cover the distance physically, meaning traffic congestion, road accidents and other obstacles can slow down the journey.Does Auto-Drive work with boats in GTA 6?Yes. Auto-Drive is not restricted to cars and other road vehicles. According to GTA6.house and Games.gg, players can also use the feature while travelling in boats across Leonida's waterways.
paragraph4: The process is similar to activating it in a car. Players need to get into a boat, mark a destination that can be reached through water, switch to Cinematic Mode and activate Auto-Drive using the controller.The boat will then navigate towards the selected waypoint without requiring players to steer manually. However, there is one limitation: if the destination is on land, Auto-Drive will stop once the boat reaches the end of its navigable water route.Can players use Auto-Drive in all situations?Not necessarily. The feature has certain limitations, particularly when players are involved in police pursuits or navigating difficult terrain.As per Beebom, players can access the Auto Drive setting under Settings and Gameplay and switch it to 'Unrestricted' to make the feature available in more situations. However, the driving AI can still encounter obstacles or collide with other vehicles.Auto-Drive is therefore best suited to relaxed journeys rather than situations that require quick reactions, precise manoeuvres or escaping police attention.For players who want to explore Vice City and the wider Leonida map without constantly controlling the vehicle, Auto-Drive offers another way to experience the open-world environment. It does not eliminate travel time, but it gives players the freedom to sit back and enjoy the journey.About the AuthorGarvit BhiraniGarvit Bhirani is a journalist based in Gurugram.

He is a Deputy Chief Content Producer at LiveMint, where he covers national and international news stories, focusing on accuracy and compelling storytelling for readers.

With a total of six years of experience in journalism, he has previously worked with Vaco Binary Semantics for Google, taking on the role of news curation lead, and reported from the field on health, education, and agriculture stories for 101reporters and News9. He has also served as a content editor for entertainment and news media organisations.

Garvit holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in journalism and mass communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University and Gurugram University, respectively. During college days, he joined India’s only non-profit student journalism network, where he anchored daily news updates and produced his own weekly show called ‘Data Fix’.

He was selected for the YES Foundation Media for Social Change Fellowship in Delhi, the Talking Data to the Fourth Pillar residential workshop, and the VOICE Fellowship in Pune.

He holds certificates in COVID-19-verification reporting, data journalism, food & agriculture, tech policy, media literacy and countering misinformation, and tackling election disinformation courses from Thomson Foundation, IndiaSpend, The Dialogue, US Mission in India, and AFP.

title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
title_bn: আইজাকের বাঁধন ডেভেলপার রিপেন্ট্যান্স প্লাস থেকে এআই সঙ্গীত সরিয়ে দেয়
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto
paragraph1: Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music.
paragraph2: Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto-themed section. They found several audio files with Suno metadata that pointed back to the tracks on Suno’s site.Creator Edmund McMillen took to X to apologize and claimed he “had no idea” the in-game GTA parody used generative AI music.
paragraph3: Adding to the drama, Valve requires developers to disclose how and when they use generative AI in the development process, and Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind Repentance Plus, doesn’t appear to have mentioned the AI music anywhere.Within hours of the discovery, Nicalis shared on X that Repentance Plus had been updated and the generated music files had been removed.
paragraph4: While reviews on Steam have yet to rebound, and the game is still rated as “overwhelmingly negative,” users on X seem to be giving McMillen the benefit of the doubt, likely because he’s been quite outspoken on AI in game development, calling it “uninspired and bland” in a TikTok from 2024.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
bangla_paragraph1: টেরেনস ও'ব্রায়েন হলেন ভার্জ এর উইকএন্ড সম্পাদক। তিনি ১৮ বছরেরও বেশি সময় ধরে প্রযুক্তি শিল্পের সাথে জড়িত এবং সিনথেটিক্স সম্পর্কে এক বা দুইটি জিনিস জানেন।
bangla_paragraph2: রেডডিট ব্যবহারকারী শুইটস স্টফ একটি গ্র্যান্ড চুরি অটো-থিমযুক্ত বিভাগে ব্যবহৃত গানগুলি আবিষ্কার করেছিলেন। তারা সুনোর মেটাডেটা সহ বেশ কয়েকটি অডিও ফাইল খুঁজে পেয়েছিল যা সুনো এর সাইটে ট্র্যাকগুলিকে নির্দেশ করেছিল। স্রষ্টা এডমন্ড ম্যাকমিলেন এক্সকে ক্ষমা চেয়েছিলেন এবং দাবি করেছিলেন যে তিনি কোন ধারণা ছিল না  গেম-এর জিটিএ প্যারোডিতে জেনারেটিভ এআই সংগীত ব্যবহৃত হয়েছিল।
bangla_paragraph3: নাটক যোগ করার জন্য, ভালভের বিকাশকারীদের বিকাশ প্রক্রিয়ায় কীভাবে এবং কখন তারা জেনারেটিভ এআই ব্যবহার করে তা প্রকাশ করতে হবে এবং রিপেনটেন্স প্লাসের পিছনে স্টুডিও নিকালিস, ইনক। কোথাও এআই সংগীত উল্লেখ করেনি বলে মনে হচ্ছে। আবিষ্কারের কয়েক ঘন্টার মধ্যে, নিকালিজ এক্স-এ ভাগ করেছেন যে রিপেইন্টেন্স প্লাসে আপডেট করা হয়েছে এবং উত্পন্ন সংগীত ফাইলগুলি সরানো হয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph4: যদিও স্টিমে পর্যালোচনাগুলি এখনও পুনরুদ্ধার হয়নি, এবং গেমটি এখনও অত্যন্ত নেতিবাচক হিসাবে রেট করা হয়েছে, এক্স-এর ব্যবহারকারীরা মনে হয় ম্যাকমিলেনকে সন্দেহের সুবিধা দিচ্ছেন, সম্ভবত কারণ তিনি গেম বিকাশের ক্ষেত্রে এআই সম্পর্কে বেশ স্পষ্ট ছিলেন, এটিকে আনুপ্রাণিত এবং বেহাল বলে অভিহিত করেছেন ২০২৪ থেকে একটি টিকটকে। আপনার ব্যক্তিগতকৃত হোমপেজে ফিডে আরও দেখতে এবং ইমেল আপডেট পেতে এই গল্পের বিষয় এবং লেখকদের অনুসরণ করুন।

title: TechCrunch Mobility: A/B testing robots vs. humans
title_bn: টেকক্রাঞ্চ মোবিলিটিঃ এ/বি টেস্টিং রোবট বনাম মানুষ
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and, now more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
paragraph1: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and, now more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility! Waymo pulling its robotaxis off freeways (again) and Zoox robotaxis launching on the Uber app illustrate the push and pull between progress and setbacks in the autonomous vehicle industry. There are signs of growth. For instance, Tesla has now surpassed Waymo in Texas in the number of robotaxis registered with the state (Tesla has 1,507 and Waymo has 1,345). But does that translate to market dominance? A better metric, if we’re trying to gauge who is leading, would be commercial driverless miles. And if we’re measuring cost-efficiency, another useful metric would be driverless miles per vehicle. By those measures, Waymo is still ahead, based on data available to me. But with Waymo’s recent freeways setback and Tesla’s push to expand its robotaxi fleet with Cybercabs, that lead could shrink. Not that there needs to be a winner, by the way. Transportation is deeply fragmented, and there is room for multiple players in the U.S., not to mention the rest of the world. A/B test: humans vs. robots A recent discussion with my Autonocast co-host Ed Niedermeyer, whose book, “Elon Take the Wheel,” comes out December 1, got me thinking about how Las Vegas could soon become a real world A/B test of sorts for human-driven vs.
paragraph2: autonomous ride-hailing services. Uber, as mentioned above, just added Zoox to its ride-hailing app in Las Vegas. For now, riders don’t have much of a choice. Uber customers can increase their chances of getting a Zoox robotaxi, and they can always decline a robot ride. But they can’t directly select a robotaxi. Instead, Uber riders will be matched with one if it’s available. Uber said that will soon change. The company plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in its app as “availability and reliability improve,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call in November. Las Vegas will also become the first U.S. city where riders can access two fully driverless partners through the Uber app, he said. (Hyundai’s self-driving subsidiary Motional is also an Uber partner.) That would give Uber riders a meaningful choice: a human driver or a robotaxi, and potentially even which autonomous service to use. And it could offer a revealing look at what customers actually prefer when given that choice. Price could tip the balance, too. It makes me wonder whether Las Vegas will become the next battleground for organized labor as robotaxis begin competing directly with human drivers.
paragraph3: A little bird Image Credits:Bryce Durbin You might have seen the Wall Street Journal scoop that General Motors is working with an executive search firm to identify possible candidates to replace CEO Mary Barra. Rumors of her imminent departure have swirled for months, but this time there appears to be real work happening behind the scenes. I reached out to a few little birds to learn more and here’s what they’re telling me. And, for the record, GM declined to comment. GM has hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles, according to one source, who noted it’s possible that the board has other executive search firms working on this as well. The board is taking a two-track approach to its search, which is occurring simultaneously. The first is focused on traditional yet transformative automotive CEOs. One name that has come up from the executive search firm is José Muñoz, who is president and CEO of Hyundai. The board is also interested in someone less traditional. The firm has apparently floated names like Doug Field, who recently became CEO of Mind Robotics, and Larry Culp of GE, according to a source with direct information. There are internal GM folks who are also in the mix, including Sterling Anderson, co-founder of self-driving trucks company Aurora who became chief product officer at GM in May 2025, and Paul Jacobson, the company’s executive vice president and chief financial officer. Got a tip for us? Email Kirsten Korosec at [email protected]. Deals! Image Credits:Bryce Durbin Elysian Aircraft, the Dutch aerospace company developing aviation electrification technologies, raised €12 million in private and public funding from FideFlux, SecFund, and ROM InWest, as well as from individual investors and family offices. Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, an electric three-wheeler business under Mahindra & Mahindra, is looking at an IPO in about 18 months, per Bloomberg.
paragraph4: Numa, a startup developing an AI operating system for dealerships, raised a $45 million Series C round led by New York-based Blue Cloud Ventures. Threshold Ventures, Costanoa, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures, and Tokio Marine Future Fund also participated. Stark Future, a European electric motorcycle company, raised at least €150 million in equity, Reuters reported. The raise was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s 1GT and Axon Partners Group. Vincue, an automotive tech company that sells software to dealerships, raised $93 million in a round led by Wavecrest Growth Partners, with continued backing from FM Capital. Notable reads and other tidbits Image Credits:Bryce Durbin Also, the electric micromobility startup that spun out of Rivian last year, has paused deliveries of its new e-bike over problems with its software and batteries, The Verge reported. Edmunds released new data that found the average new vehicle is selling for a record $50,087. Redwood Materials is using computer vision and machine learning to identify and sort batteries by chemistry before they’re fed into the company’s rotary calciner — a massive cylindrical industrial furnace used to process 40,000 metric tons of raw feedstock a year. Tesla said it will spend about $3.3 billion to expand its Berlin gigafactory to produce Cybercabs — yet another signal of the company’s global autonomy ambitions. Over the weekend, Tesla invited “select customers” to preorder the company’s autonomous, golden Cybercab “for personal use.” The Cybercab is priced at $29,990, but there is a lot more to ownership. The company will charge owners $299 a month to use the vehicles, delivery will only occur in a handful of cities, and operations will be limited to specific locations. Uber opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities.
paragraph5: Uber already has a service for teenagers. If this program proves successful, it would open Uber up to another market of customers: busy families. Meanwhile, Uber said it’s notifying close to 150,000 drivers that their personal information was stolen in an October data breach. Zipline continues to scale its autonomous drone delivery business, this time in its partnership with Uber. The companies had previously announced a partnership for drones to deliver for Uber Eats, but it officially launched this week in a Houston suburb. The aim is a big one: Uber and Zipline say they aim to make 1 million deliveries a day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029. One more thing … I had a chance to catch up with (and interview) Ro Gupta, the head of Woven Capital — Toyota’s growth fund. I’ve known Gupta for years; we first met when I worked at Fortune and he had a startup called Carmera. A lot has happened since those AV 1.0 days, and Gupta caught us up on this next era of AV innovation and where Toyota is interested in investing. It’s not enough to simply state “AI.” There’s more to it than that. Take a listen. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.
